ordered_diagnoses: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with liver dysfunction and a large cystic tumor
salient_findings: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transferase
Large, multilocular cystic tumor in the liver with solid components
Depressed liver function indicated by indocyanine green plasma disappearance rate
key_facts: 65-year-old woman presented with right dorsal pain
Total bilirubin 1.3 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 452 IU/L
γ-glutamyl transferase 167 IU/L
Indocyanine green plasma disappearance rate was 0.103
15-minute retention rate was 23.9%
Tests for hepatitis B and C viral markers were negative
Abdominal CT revealed a well-defined, low-density, heterogeneous, multilocular cystic tumor
Tumor measured 16 cm in diameter and compressed the umbilical portion of the portal vein, the right portal vein, and the left hepatic vein
MRI showed mixed high and low signal intensity
PET–CT showed FDG uptake in the solid components of the cyst

shortlist: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Multilocular cystic tumor with solid components and high CA125 levels

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Large cystic tumor with solid components and high FDG uptake on PET-CT

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic tumor with septa and solid components, similar to mucinous cystadenocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Hepatic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large cystic tumor with solid components and aggressive features

shortlist.label: Hepatoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare liver tumor with cystic and solid components, although less likely in a 65-year-old woman

raw.rationale: The patient's abdominal CT and MRI findings of a multilocular cystic tumor with septa and solid components, along with the presence of mucinous content and hemorrhage, are consistent with mucinous cystadenocarcinoma. The tumor's size, location, and compression of nearby vessels also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
rejected.why: While the patient's tumor has solid components, the presence of mucinous content and the tumor's multilocular cystic appearance are more characteristic of mucinous cystadenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor does not have the typical features of biliary cystadenocarcinoma, such as a prominent ovarian-like stroma.

rejected.label: Hepatic sarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor has a more complex appearance with mucinous content and hemorrhage, which is not typical of hepatic sarcoma.

rejected.label: Hepatoblastoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and tumor characteristics are not consistent with hepatoblastoma, which is typically seen in children and has a distinct histological appearance.
